scenarios.description: You sent an important work email to a colleague 3 days ago asking for their input on a project deadline. They haven't responded yet, and you know they usually check email regularly. The deadline is approaching and their input would be very helpful.
scenarios.question: Why do you think your colleague hasn't responded to your email?

hostile.text: They're deliberately ignoring me because they don't want to help or think my request isn't important

neutral.text: They're probably busy with other priorities and haven't had time to respond yet

benign.text: They might have missed the email or are waiting to gather the right information before responding

scenarios.description: During a team meeting, you're presenting an idea that you've worked hard on. A colleague interrupts you mid-sentence to point out a potential problem with your proposal. They speak in a direct tone and continue to ask several challenging questions about your approach.
scenarios.question: Why do you think your colleague interrupted and challenged your idea?

hostile.text: They want to undermine me or make me look bad in front of the team

neutral.text: They're being direct about business concerns and want to ensure we consider all angles

benign.text: They're trying to help improve the idea by identifying potential issues early

instructions: Read each scenario carefully and choose the explanation that best describes why you think the person acted that way. Consider their likely intentions and motivations.
